title: Making male friends
reason: 从昨日的软件与数字生活主题轮换到日常生活和人际沟通。节目讨论维持友谊、在困难时期相互支持以及成年后关系逐渐疏远，适合联系远程协作、跨团队关系和工程管理中的支持网络；练习围绕六个高频表达重复调用，从原文支撑逐步过渡到改写、受限工作场景应用和有限自由表达。

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does it mean to share life's ups and downs with a friend?

options.text: To support each other through good and difficult experiences.
To compete over who has the harder life.
To meet only when everything is going well.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Beth says everyone needs friends to share life's ups and downs, meaning both positive and difficult experiences.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the reusable relationship phrase: Regular contact can help people ______ even when they live far apart.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme discusses how people make and keep close friends; 'maintain strong friendships' means keep those relationships healthy over time.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: According to Claudia Hammond, what do good friends often do when times are tough?

options.text: They listen, reassure and sometimes offer advice.
They end the friendship until the problem is over.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Claudia says friends are there to listen, reassure and perhaps advise us during periods of trouble.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the transcript-based idea: Friends can help us ______ difficult periods of life.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil explains that friends help us get through difficult periods, meaning manage to live through them.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: If two friends have drifted away, what has happened?

options.text: They have gradually become less close.
They have immediately become business partners.
They have planned a trip together.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript defines 'drift away' as gradually moving apart until the connection weakens or breaks.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Max's description: Being the public face of a book called 'Billy No-Mates' was ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Max uses this exact phrase because the memorable title brought both favourable and unfavourable consequences.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why can social media make loneliness feel worse for some younger men?

options.text: It can make it look as if everyone else is enjoying time with friends.
It guarantees that users will maintain close friendships.
It only shows information about elderly people.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says social media can make it seem that everyone else is having a great time with their mates except you.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the warning about relationships: Without regular contact, close friends can gradually ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: This lightly transfers the transcript's explanation that friends can gradually move apart until their connection breaks.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Retell the episode in 80-120 words without looking at the full transcript. Use this structure: (1) topic - why making and keeping close male friends can be difficult; (2) two key ideas - how friends help during hard times and how relationships can gradually weaken; (3) conclusion or example - Max Dickins's experience and one possible way to meet people. Phrase bank: 'when times are tough', 'drift away', 'a double-edged sword'. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, clear English is enough; advanced vocabulary and complex sentences are not required.
referencePoints: Close friends are important for sharing both good and difficult experiences and supporting mental wellbeing.
Friends can listen, reassure and advise us, helping us get through difficult periods.
The programme discusses a stereotype that men may be less likely to nurture friendships and may gradually drift away from friends.
Max Dickins realised he had no close male friend to ask to be his best man and wrote the book 'Billy No-Mates'.
The book title was a double-edged sword because it was memorable but publicly connected Max with having no friends.
Max suggests meeting people in third spaces such as sports clubs or reading groups, separate from home and work.
